newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says it has killed seven Iraq-based rebels.
newsitem.headline: Iran says it has killed seven Iraq-based rebels.

text.p: Iranian security forces have killed seven members of an Iraq-based armed opposition group in two separate clashes, Iran's official news agency IRNA said on Monday.

It quoted the Intelligence (internal security) Ministry as saying police and security agents on Monday killed three Mujahideen Khalq members, a woman and two men, in a shootout in Sari, 110 km (70 miles) northeast of Tehran.

A local official in the town of Mehran near the Iraqi border said government forces killed four Mujahideen members after they crossed into Iran, the agency reported. It did not say when the four were killed.
Government forces also seized arms, explosives and cyanide pills from the two Mujahideen teams which the agency said had entered the country to carry out sabotage operations.

Tehran has said its troops killed several Mujahideen members in clashes in western Iran in the past few weeks. The Mujahideen have admitted that some of their forces were killed but said they had slain dozens of government troops.
Iran has not reported any casualties among its forces.

Tehran has blamed the group, which has several camps in Iraq near the Iranian border, for cross-border attacks and bombings in the past few years. The Mujahideen have denied attacking civilians, but have taken responsibility for hitting military, government and military targets.
